proposed_by: the pause design «pauza vocii» (voice-continuous timing), after the Owner listened to the before/after preview built from the takes already paid for
owner_decision: 2026-10-16, the Owner, after the preview: «Sună foarte bine și este o îmbunătățire. Deci da.» One take per writer scene and per speaker run; joins by class from each voice's own pauses; marked beats; END = the narrator's PARAGRAPH pause; tempo 1.0 per channel; the trim to the last letter with its guard; nothing hard-coded.
note: A proposal the Owner may change; it is not in his database. backend/app/media/pauses.py holds only the formulas: every number they use is here, each research constant with its source and each studio choice with its reason. The per-channel knobs (tempo, where the picture cut falls inside a pause, the L-cut, the film's end) are in config/factual_look.json and config/serial_series_look.json under "pauses"; channel_defaults below is what a look file that names none gets. Each voice's own numbers are measured from its kept PAID narration takes (<media_root>/<film>/narration/*.json, the vendor's 'alignment', never 'normalized_alignment') and cached in the git-ignored <media_root>/voice_pause_profiles.json; a voice with fewer than min_samples of a pause takes its pool's, and a pool with too few takes the fallback below. Each film's pauses are frozen on its storyboard rows when it is built, so a later change here never changes an open film. With use_until_the_owner_changes_it false the studio keeps its legacy timing (0.4 s after every shot, the old trim).

trim_to_last_letter.why: The vendor stretches a take's final '.' to the end of its file and the old trim let the vendor's clock veto the meter: it cut 0.000 s on all 55 kept takes. The take is now cut at its last letter or digit (+ 0.03 s), guarded so that no sound is split (assembler._trimmed_take, pauses.trim_cut); only then is a planned pause the silence heard.

voice_groups.why: One take per writer scene (factual) and per speaker run inside a beat (serial); the montage cuts the picture on the word timestamps inside it and adds 0 s.

marked_beats.why: The Owner, 2026-10-16: a writer's «…» at a factual scene's end, «(beat)» in a serial direction, is a real silence.

per_take_tempo.why: A take's own pace comes from its text (numbers, short takes) at a fixed vendor speed, not from the voice: scaling pauses by it is off (Trouvain 2004: the effect varies by speaker).

paragraph_ratio.source: Doukhan et al. 2012 (Interspeech): a professional storyteller reading 12 tales paused 1127 ms at a paragraph against 720 ms at a sentence (median), 1.565; Strangert 1991 gives 1/0.6 = 1.67.

turn_seconds.source: Stivers et al. 2009 (PNAS, 10 languages): the English mean gap at a speaker change, 236 ms; Heldner & Edlund 2010: gaps between speakers are shorter than pauses within one; Templeton 2022: longer gaps were rated less enjoyable.

turn_floor_seconds.source: Heldner 2011 (JASA, detection thresholds for gaps and overlaps): a silence between speakers under about 120 ms is not heard as a gap. Heldner & Edlund 2010 (three corpora) is the related measurement of where real transitions fall.

beat_floor_seconds.source: Kendrick & Torreira 2015: a gap of 700 ms or more reads as marked (dispreferred responses only outnumber preferred ones from 700 ms).

beat_ceiling_seconds.source: Roberts et al. 2006: silences of 600 and 1200 ms change what a response means; Frontiers in Psychology 2022: past a 1.2 s pause naturalness falls.

beat_factor.source: Televised stand-up (828 performances, arXiv 2605.00143): the pause before the highest-surprise sentence was 35.6-41% longer than before low-surprise ones. Tunable.

join_ceiling_seconds.source: Frontiers in Psychology 2022 (English read speech, pauses at commas and periods changed): past a 1.2 s period pause, rated naturalness falls. Every planned join except a card stays at or under it.

short_guard_syllables.source: Zvonik & Cummins 2003 (1212 inter-sentence pauses, six speakers): pauses under about 300 ms occurred essentially only next to a phrase of 10 syllables or fewer. Two short neighbouring sentences take the voice's first-quartile pause.

dead_air_tolerance.source: Owoicho et al. 2024 (Speech Prosody): listeners notice inter-sentence pauses only far from the norm; 0.2 is their Weber example. A join heard longer than planned x (1 + this) + one frame is dead air.

no_pause_before_a_punchline.source: Attardo & Pickering 2011: in 20 joke performances speakers neither paused before the punchline nor changed speech rate around it.

min_samples.why: A voice's own pause (or its high speech rate) is used from 5 measured samples; under that its pool's (Nadia had 3 sentence pauses on 2026-10-16).

realised_pause_seconds.why: A comma is paused only about half the time (narrator 45%): the clause pause is read where the voice did pause, from the measurement's own detection minimum (silencedetect d = 0.08 s, 2026-10-16).

body_pair.why: The factual body alternates these two purposes scene by scene; a change between them is no new section (a PARAGRAPH at every cut of a five-scene film was rejected).

factual.why: The writer's ellipsis at the end of a scene: «…» asks for a silence after it.

serial_words.why: A serial line's direction that asks for a silence («(beat)», "long pause"), matched as whole words.

marks_per_section.why: The Owner, 2026-10-16: at most one marked silence per factual section or serial beat.

wall_cap_seconds.why: YouTube's Shorts wall: the wall is min(the channel's shorts_max_seconds, this).

wall_stages.why: Speakers shorten pauses first when they speed up (Trouvain 2004; Werner 2022) and shorter pauses were not dispreferred (Owoicho 2024): the row-voiced clause and dash pauses go toward their floors first, then one common factor shrinks every join's distance to its floor, so the ladder keeps its order.

never_compressed.why: A marked silence is the writer's, and a silent card's length is already its pause.

rate_spread.why: The narrator's per-take speech rate, first quartile over median (2.696 / 2.982 spoken words a second, 25 takes, 2026-10-16; 0.912 counted in written words): a voice with fewer than min_samples takes has its high rate (what a clip is bought for) from its median and this spread, until its pool can measure its own.

tempo.why: The Owner, 2026-10-16: every pause follows the voice's own rhythm (1.0); a channel may make it brisker or calmer in its look file.

cut_in_pause.why: Where the picture cut falls inside a pause: 1.0, the outgoing shot holds the whole pause and the new picture comes with its words, as before. The Owner may choose 0.1 (Leake 2017).

picture_slide_words.why: No L-cut: the picture cuts on the words until the Owner asks the picture to flow a word over the next phrase.

end_class.why: The Owner, 2026-10-16: the film's last word is held for the narrator's PARAGRAPH pause (about 0.77 s), the serial included.

fallback.provenance: 2026-10-16 measurement of the 55 kept eleven_flash_v2 takes of 8 films (25 narrator, 30 serial characters). Pauses: ffmpeg silencedetect at -45 dB, zeros included (the clause pause where the voice paused). Speech rate: from the first letter to the last on the vendor's alignment, a word counted as assembler.spoken_words counts it (a number said in words), the unit every estimate multiplies; seconds_per_word_high is 1 / the takes' first-quartile rate.
